author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Springworks Farm lettuce has disappeared from Hannaford shelves in New Hampshire and across the supermarket chain’s regional footprint, while the status of the Lisbon, Maine, aquaponics business remains unclear.

Manchester Ink Link reported that Springworks stopped supplying Hannaford and other customers weeks ago. The farm’s phone was disconnected, employees did not respond to outreach and its website no longer displayed a store-locator page. Hannaford had not provided a public explanation before the outlet’s deadline.

Springworks had been Hannaford’s exclusive supplier of organic romaine for all 184 stores in New England and New York. Founded in 2014 by Trevor Kenkel, the company used aquaponics, combining greenhouse crops with recirculating water from fish production. By 2024, its products reportedly reached about 300 stores and institutions, including Whole Foods, Roche Bros., Food City, Sysco Northern New England and Maine schools.

The company announced $22 million in financing in 2023 for a new greenhouse, but the current status of that expansion was not established in the report. The available evidence shows a halt in retail supply, not a confirmed permanent closure.
dek: The Maine aquaponics grower that supplied organic romaine across Hannaford’s footprint has stopped appearing on store shelves, with its business status unresolved.
headline: Springworks lettuce disappears from Hannaford as farm status remains unclear
